title: Goodbye Deponia
text: :  It's a good point and click adventure.  I absolutely recommend if it's on sale.  Whether you want to pay full price is up to how much of a point and click enthusiast you are. : Now with more Rufus than most can handle; this Deponia is extremely heavy on the dialogue but takes the puzzles and misadventures to the next level.  Many point and click adventures have degrees of moon logic where a nonsensical combination of items and actions somehow solves the problem, but Deponia makes it somehow seem almost rational in hindsight.  Rufus often made me simultaneously gasp in horror and laugh at some of the stunts he pulled on his fellow Deponians. :  It has a moderate amount of pixel hunting.  Some of the scenes are extremely cluttered and can make finding the one thing needed difficult.  The puzzles in Goodbye Deponia are much trickier, which I found to be both more satisfying and more frustrating at times.  Expect patient trial and error spotting the hidden patterns or occasional google searches.

title: Goodbye Deponia
text: This is a solid continuation of the story presented in the first two games, but unfortunately a poor ending to the otherwise (mostly) excellent Deponia series. The ending is unsatisfying and leaves far too many story threads hanging to provide real closure for the story. On the other hand, it leaves things wide open for a Deponia 4, but it appears the chances of that happening at this point are very close to 0. Poor ending aside, the story was mostly great, but some of the puzzle solutions were a bit dark for my tastes. I get that Rufus is supposed to be a jerk, but some of the solutions go far beyond that. From a technical standpoint, it's a huge step up from the earlier games. In both the earlier titles I had a lot of problems with minigames not working at all (and even a complete game breaking bug in the first game that required downloading an official savegame file to fix) but this one worked flawlessly. The puzzle difficulty is about right (although as with any adventure game some of the solutions are so random and obtuse that you'll probably spend a significant amount of time with trial and error unless you use a guide). Overall, I enjoyed the ride I had with the series (in spite of the ending) and can easily recommend it if you're at all interested in adventure games. Make sure to get the whole series in a discounted bundle (happens semi regularly).

text: This is a fantastic hidden picutre/puzzle adventure games. While the story is cliche and overly predictable, the outstanding audio and visual presentation, whimsical setting and solid design more than make up for it. The puzzle variety remains unique and interesting throughout without ever getting to difficult or frustrating. The hidden picture portion is also stays fresh due to the combining elements mechanic which has you building certain objects before you can finish finding them. The adventure gameplay elements are well done and the hint hourglass has a low enough cool down that you will never feel lost or frustrated. If you like this genre, or you just want to play a beautiful, relaxing advenure game, this is an absolute must play. GG!

title: Gun Metal
text: Warning: This is a very old game (2002, now 14 years old) and has aspect ratio issues. Normally when a game has dated too much I find it difficult to provide a thumbs up.  Gun Metal is a cautious exception. The developers have done well enough with the game that it runs with no showstopping issues under Windows 10.   It's somewhat simplistic for todays standard, but the game is distinctive because it's the almost the only PC game that allows you to operate a tranforming mecha/fighter (think Macross). It lacks a lot of the cool eastern aesthetic of the Macross series, but the gameplay is very fun once you get into it, although it's almost arcadelike in the simplicity.  The developers did an exceptional job of allowing you to upgrade your mecha with different weapons as you progress, as well as providing an action environment where it makes sense for you to switch in and out of vehicle mode to exploit the various strengths and weaknesses of your fighting machine.

title: GunZ 2: The Second Duel
text: Great game for the elitist gamer extraordinaire.  I'm no Master of Epeendom so I died in the tutorial haha If you're used to the shift key being for sprint this will be tricky for ya, was for me.  Shift is for guard in this, and then there are these key combos of tap space then tap w twice or press space multiple times to climb a wall, not bad, but takes some getting used to. The tutorial isn't enough for slow folks like me to get acclimated to the game environment.  When I died the game said "continue" while counting off from 10 to 0, I pressed enter, left clicked, right clicked, nothing seemed to work to continue, and, since the guys hitting me took 90% of my health in one hit, I realize I'm not out to play a stressy "campaign." Gone it seems are the days of a challenging games, without just making it all about shear force or key combos, games with a decent story, puzzles to complete to gain a permanent bonus or skill on top of what you'd normally have and usually from, or as an incentive for, talomg a different path exploring.  Stress comes from concern of losing your progress if you die from a mob that, if there were more than one of them you wouldn't make it.  No more games with stories that walk you through the gameplay to learn versus just run you through so you can forget more than you remember and let down teammates.  This really could be fun to play, but clearly this game is for a small market, and as a previous reviewer said, "the game is dying," maybe the developers just want it that way. Sure it's a shooter, yet, that doesn't mean it can't have a story or any of that, I figure it's just a Korean game appealing to Korean players in a country where gaming is a significan't national sport, for the most part, thus void of consideration for more casual  players or the full range of possibilities for their game that would bring in a larger range of players as well.

title: GunZ 2: The Second Duel
text: Gunz 2 tries to re-invent the original Gunz so many years ago, and succeeds,  in both good ways and bad. The Korean game developer has created a somewhat fun game to play, that is burdened with a few heavy problems, mostly related to the economy of the game. The visuals, combat, and smoothness of the game have all been improved, but it still maintains some of the bigger problems most F2P games are trying to move out of these days. The premium weapons and gear are simple much better than what you get without, and in a versus match, that is not exactly pleasant for those not spending the cash. Also, for those that do go and pay premium, items have time limits restrictions such as a day or two or hours. The game also removes the versatiltiy of the original gunz, the ability to really make your own character and playstyle. Gunz 2 offers some very nice classes, that all play differently and have some nice voice actros backing them. The issue is you get one type of loadout, an example is one character has a sword, SMG, and a sniper rifle, and that is IT. You can upgrade them to various versions, however you cannot change your characters playstyle at all. There are 4 to choose from. The grahpics are outdated to todays standards, but anyone who played the original gunz knows this is intentional as they want it to run on as many machines as possible. There is one new feature that really makes this more enjoyable than the original in one way. They added skills. As you level up you will unlock a few different skills that can be used in battle, allowing you to roundhouse kick people, perform parry-attack counters, etc.... To sumamrize: The Good: -Improved visuals, gameplay performance -Fluid combat, fun to use swords and guns -More user friendly than original in some ways -Addition of skills and mission modes with boses adds more variety than the original had The Bad: -Premium items are more powerful than their non premium counterparts -Premium items have time limitations so you have to keep buying them. -Time related items -Heavy balance issues -Hits and such do not feel very satisfying -non premium users can upgrade their limited weapon selection, however they do not have many choices right now. -They took away the custom playstyles of the original and force you into 1 of four catagories instead. You can no longer use the guns and melee weapons you like, you have to choose one of these 4 presets instead. -The korean company has been known to ban people for silly reasons, AND I DEFEND MOST COMPANIES WHEN THEY BAN, but this company actually banned people because they got caught in bugs in early access and couldn't get out, like wall bugs and such. You fix them, you don't ban people unless they are openly exploiting... -Early access game, but already has hacks out on the net. -The game is simply an improved version of the old one, with better combat, but less of the things that made the original great. -When characters die and such, there are only foru and they all seem to only have one voice line for thigns. So in a death match all you hear is like "UGHH I'm not done yet" CONSTANTLY lol. -Melee combat is just a cluttered stun fest -the game lags upon death 6/10, the game is good and playable and the new skills are cool, the power of premium, lack of custom playstyles, and few upgrade options make it not the best game on the market. ~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~ WARNING EDIT: They actually patched this game and managed to make it a little worse, I would currently give it a 3.5/10 barely...and thus, it is no longer a recommended title.

title: GunZ 2: The Second Duel
text: - Laggy due to peer to peer (p2p) connection, so host always has the upper hand. - Costly store items, i.e. one revive coin = $2.50, $15 for a mask, - Possibly pay to win (p2w)- $36 for beginner items, which include weapons that have different (maybe higher?) stats. - AI is OP in co-op games, they can stun lock you and do insane damage. - Guy with big shield has no real added defense vs other players. - Combat is lackluster, doesn't feel as fluid as part 1 did. - Servers suck for login, sitting at the "push any key" waiting for the server to see I pushed ANY key. Also waiting up to 2minutes at "start" for a mission/match can be really tiresum. Even the lobby room lags due to poor servers. Given this game was in open beta during 2011 in korea this game shouldn't be this buggy. I may try this game out later when more love is put into it but as of right now it's not worth the hastle to even log into the game.
